### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bfbc4edc7fe6e75e2310913b34a2f4f62d6e33c`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bfbc4edc7fe6e75e2310913b34a2f4f62d6e33c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `adc0290b8e8e1ca54b85a2569824d4792c40145b` — the merge of head `d0a5a29e996e936939df0ca0fa42af498a0e8608` into base `8bfbc4edc7fe6e75e2310913b34a2f4f62d6e33c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin adc0290b8e8e1ca54b85a2569824d4792c40145b && git checkout adc0290b8e8e1ca54b85a2569824d4792c40145b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8bfbc4edc7fe6e75e2310913b34a2f4f62d6e33c d0a5a29e996e936939df0ca0fa42af498a0e8608 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8bfbc4edc7fe6e75e2310913b34a2f4f62d6e33c && git merge --no-ff d0a5a29e996e936939df0ca0fa42af498a0e8608

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bfbc4edc7fe6e75e2310913b34a2f4f62d6e33c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8bfbc4edc7fe6e75e2310913b34a2f4f62d6e33c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Premise, measured by the seat:** on `origin/main` `invalidateForForeignWrite` = `deleteRegistryEntries` + `invalidateListCache` only. The diff leaves it unchanged and adds the removal step before it, keyed on the explicit `removal` marker that `unregisterAt` alone sets. `ClusterMetadataChangedPayload` is not re-exported from `packages/metadata/src/index.ts` (0 hits), so the new optional field is no published surface.
- **Clause-② (the dev's open question):** the seat keeps `Clause-②: no` (option A). The observable narrowing (a removed door item stops answering) was declared BREAKING by #32493 on the acting node; this PR restores the cluster invariant so every node gives that declared answer. No accept set of what an author or client may write changes. No `(narrowing)` arm, so no dogfood battery or contract-review-tier record is owed.
- **Pins:** 26 new cases. Each of the 4 negative pins has an ablation that turns it red (A1–A5, listed in the PR body), and the BASE run reverses all 16 positive pins. The first A1/A2 run had a vacuous pin, which was caught and repaired; that correction is recorded in the PR body.
- **Accepted deviations:** `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` sits outside the claimed surface. It documents the payload shape this PR changes, so os-dev.md rule 3 requires the edit. Sentences checked against the diff: the payload line `removal, // unregister()'s \`deleted\` event only: { packageId? }`, and the receipt paragraph ("the peer deletes its own in-memory copy by the same key … The peer never deletes from the shared store"). Both match the code. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI (`Lint · ESLint`). Changeset sentences checked against the diff and they match.
- **Out of scope:** `notify: false` removals and a lost hint after a bus outage are pre-existing and unchanged. Both are recorded under Acceptance notes and filed nowhere, since neither falls in the three filing classes.
- **Landing:** CI was in progress at this record. Readying and auto-merge happen once every check on this head is green or an expected skip.
